description:
Wesam Saad connects readiness for marriage with the character a person should seek in a future spouse. Choosing a partner, he argues, should serve a shared desire to honour God and advance His kingdom. Proverbs 12:4 and Proverbs 31 frame the search for an excellent wife rather than the bare minimum of a Christian profession. For young men, readiness includes working hard, providing generously, taking initiative in prayer and teaching, and valuing relationships within the family. Drawing on 1 Peter 3:7, he emphasises understanding and honour rather than an outgoing personality. He also clarifies that Christ alone is the believer’s mediator; a husband’s responsibilities do not make him spiritually indispensable to his wife.

The discussion then considers the qualities Wesam urges young women to cultivate: care for children, sensible judgement, purity, kindness, working at home and a willing response to authority. He asks parents to train these dispositions before marriage and encourages prospective spouses to notice how they already appear in daily life. Throughout, he distinguishes genuine commitment to biblical principles from sinless perfection. Listeners are urged to prepare faithfully, work hard and build family relationships, while trusting God rather than rushing anxiously into marriage when no suitable partner is present.

questions.question: What connects readiness for marriage with choosing a spouse?
questions.answer: Wesam treats the two questions as overlapping. The qualities that show a person is ready for marriage also help someone of the opposite sex recognise a suitable spouse. He places the shared desire to honour God and advance His kingdom ahead of personal preferences.

questions.question: Why does Wesam draw attention to the excellent wife in Proverbs?
questions.answer: He uses Proverbs 12:4 and Proverbs 31 to argue against settling for a bare Christian profession. A prospective spouse should look for character that will support a godly marriage, and he applies the corresponding expectation to the search for an excellent husband.

questions.question: How should a young man learn to become a provider?
questions.answer: Wesam says training involves more than earning money. Young men should learn to work hard and use what they earn generously, placing the needs of their family and church ahead of their own preferences. Parents should cultivate that pattern gradually through real responsibilities.

questions.question: What does spiritual initiative mean here, and what limit does Wesam place on a husband’s role?
questions.answer: He urges men to pray for their families and willingly teach God’s word instead of depending on constant reminders. His language about a husband being a priest and prophet describes responsibility, not a replacement for Christ. He explicitly says that Jesus Christ alone is the believer’s mediator and high priest.

questions.question: Does being relational require an outgoing personality?
questions.answer: Wesam says it does not. Appealing to 1 Peter 3:7, he stresses understanding, honour and a high view of commitment to family members. The issue is whether a young man wants to know and care for the people he lives with rather than treating home merely as a place to eat, sleep and use a screen.

questions.question: What qualities does Wesam encourage young women to develop before marriage?
questions.answer: He discusses care for children, including a desire to teach them about God, sensible judgement, purity, kindness, working at home and willingness to respond to a father’s authority. He urges prospective husbands and parents to consider the direction already visible in a woman’s life, while acknowledging that maturity is a matter of degree.

questions.question: Must a person become perfect before marrying?
questions.answer: Wesam explicitly rejects that requirement. He distinguishes two imperfect people who embrace biblical principles from two people who enter marriage without those commitments. Marriage will expose selfishness and require growth; the question is whether each person already desires to live by those principles.

questions.question: How should someone respond when no suitable spouse is presently available?
questions.answer: Wesam encourages preparation, trust in God and freedom from anxious pressure. Searching through appropriate channels is permitted, but he does not make searching everywhere a duty. He urges listeners to enjoy fellowship with God and other believers rather than rushing into a decision they may regret.
